deep.reconstruction:
CONTEXT. The previous page traces paraxial rays through a five-element instrument (objective plus a four-lens terrestrial eyepiece). It uses the alternating recurrences gamma^(k+1) = h^(k) delta^(k) - gamma^(k) and delta^(k+1) = f^(k+1) gamma^(k+1) - delta^(k), i.e. Gaussian brackets / continuants. This page applies the same machinery to a concrete telescope whose numbers appear here.

(A) Top table, headed (b+b')gamma', (b'+b'')gamma'', (b''+b''')gamma''', (b'''+b^IV)gamma^IV. Three columns of numbers are given: (+608, -2430, +757, +1543), (+452, +182, -888, +302) and (+275, -442, -673, +46). The middle column is the previous page's gamma', gamma'', gamma''', gamma^IV at x=0 (451.8, 181.9, -887.1, 302.2), rounded. The other two columns are presumably the gammas for two other configurations, perhaps other lens orders from the previous page's table D II, C III, B IV, A V. The header is a weighted sum Sum (b_i+b_{i+1}) gamma_i, most plausibly a colour-type correction condition for the eyepiece. The meaning of b and of the outer columns is not determinable from this page.

(B) Eyepiece data. Focal lengths are 58.5, 84.2, 83.7, 70.2, listed from the eye lens toward the objective. Separations are 110.4, 140.7, 85.7 (the third is written 'B5.7' = 85.7, not 135.7). The objective focal length is 786.6.

(C) Conjugate-point chain, worked backward from the eye with the object at infinity, using 1/s + 1/s' = 1/f.
- Eye lens f=58.5: s = infinity gives s' = 58.5.
- Then 110.4 - 58.5 = 51.9.
- Lens f=84.2: 1/51.9 + 1/(-135.3) = 1/84.2.
- Then 140.7 + 135.3 = 276.0.
- Lens f=83.7: 1/276.0 + 1/120.1 = 1/83.7.
- Then 85.7 - 120.1 = -34.4.
- Lens f=70.2: 1/(-34.4) + 1/23.1 = 1/70.2.
- So the objective's focus must lie 23.1 beyond the first eyepiece lens, and the objective-to-eyepiece distance is 786.6 + 23.1 = 809.7.
- A second value, 811.5, is also written; it is probably a measured or alternative setting.

(D) Continuant check that the system is afocal (column of values beginning =+1.0000000). Work in units of 100. The coefficients are k = 100/786.6 = 0.1271294, 8.097, 100/70.2 = 1.42450, 0.857, 100/83.7 = 1.19474, 1.407, 100/84.2 = 1.18765, 1.104, 100/58.5 = 1.70940. Set x_{-1}=0, x_0=1 and apply x_{n+1} = k_n x_n - x_{n-1}. The sequence is 1, 0.1271294, 0.0293669, -0.0852963, -0.1024658, -0.0371240, +0.0502323, +0.0967817, +0.0566143, -0.0000047.

The intermediate products are scattered on the page and confirm this reading:
- 1.0293669 (= 8.097 x 0.1271294), giving the note 8097.
- 0.0418331 = 1.4245 x 0.0293669.
- 0.0730989 = 0.857 x 0.0852963.
- 0.1224203 = 1.19474 x 0.1024658.
- 0.0522335.
- 0.1068466 = 1.104 x 0.0967817.
- 7866 (= 1/0.1271294).
- Log 8.4678581 = log 0.0293669; log 9.8463371 = log(1/1.4245).

The heights and angles alternate. The final reduced angle, -0.0000047, is essentially 0: an axial parallel ray leaves parallel, confirming afocal adjustment. The exit height 0.0566143 gives angular magnification 1/0.0566143 ~ 17.7 (my inference; the page does not state it).

(E) Other material.
- 206265 (seconds per radian) and 635 (= 10'35'') link to the previous page's field-of-view and magnification estimates.
- The labels 'Ocular / Objectiv / {Galletti, Fabri, Döring}' and '(0.96)' probably assign eyepieces and objectives to particular instruments or owners.
- 'Geld' heads unrelated money sums.
- Several other columns of figures (8097/702/1077/..., 14188, 84272, 1.112, 10.534, 10.574, 11.123, 0.8287723, Gul[?]) are not reliably decodable.
errors: Rounding only: gamma''' = -887.1 is entered as -888 in the middle column.

Small accumulated rounding in the continuant: recomputation gives x7 = 0.0967823 (written 0.0967817) and final residual about -0.0000051 (written -0.0000047). Both are immaterial; the residual is about 0 either way.
Conjugate step for f=70.2: 1/(-34.4) + 1/23.1 corresponds to f = 70.3. The precise s' is 23.087, consistent with the rounded 23.1.

results.what: Conjugate-distance chain through a 4-lens terrestrial eyepiece, giving the objective-eyepiece spacing 809.7 for an infinity-focused telescope
results.modern_name: Paraxial thin-lens imaging equation applied successively (afocal telescope adjustment)

results.what: Ray trace x_{n+1} = k_n x_n - x_{n-1} through objective + 4 eyepiece lenses, with final angle about 0 checking afocality
results.modern_name: Paraxial ray-transfer recurrence / Gaussian brackets (continuants), equivalent to ABCD matrices
results.usually_credited_to: Gauss, Dioptrische Untersuchungen (1841); brackets named after Gauss

results.what: Weighted sum Sum (b_i+b_{i+1}) gamma_i evaluated for three configurations
results.modern_name: Probably a chromatic (lateral colour) correction sum for a multi-lens eyepiece
results.usually_credited_to: Euler, Klügel, Boscovich (18th-c. achromatic eyepiece theory)

deep.surprise_reason: This is a numerical application of Gauss's own paraxial (continuant) ray-tracing to a specific telescope. It is routine calculation, already Gauss's published method; there is no new theoretical result.

checkable.asserts: Image distance about 23.09 for object at -34.4 with f=70.2
Equals 7.866, objective focal length 786.6 in units of 100

transcription_corrections: '135.7' in the second column should read '85.7' (written B5.7); it is the third eyepiece separation, consistent with k = 0.857 and 85.7 - 120.1 = -34.4.
'9.0418331' is probably the number 0.0418331 (= 1.4245 x 0.0293669) rather than a logarithm.
The column '=+1.0000000 ... =-0.0000047' is one continuant sequence of alternating heights and angles, not independent equations.
